sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: In an age when almost any fact can be summoned on a telephone screen, the public library is often described as a relic, a building kept open out of sentiment rather than need. This view mistakes what libraries have always done. Their value never lay solely in the books on their shelves; it lay in offering a quiet and free space where anyone, regardless of income, could sit and think without being asked to buy anything. For a student whose home has one room and five occupants, the reading hall may be the only place where sustained concentration is possible. For an elderly pensioner, it may be the only public room in which he is welcome to linger.

The arrival of digital information has, if anything, enlarged this role. A screen offers abundance but not guidance, and the skill of judging which sources deserve trust is not acquired automatically. A trained librarian who can steer a reader from rumour towards reliable evidence performs a service that no search engine has replaced. When municipal budgets tighten, libraries are frequently the first institutions to lose staff and hours, precisely because their benefits are diffuse and difficult to count. Yet a society that closes them saves very little money and loses one of the few spaces in which citizenship, rather than purchasing power, is the only qualification for entry.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: It is often said that poetry is what gets lost in translation, and anyone who has compared a poem with its rendering in another language knows the force of the remark. Words carry not only meanings but sounds, rhythms and associations that belong to a single tongue. A word for rain in Konkani may summon the smell of wet laterite and the start of the fishing ban; its nearest English equivalent summons umbrellas and grey streets. The translator who keeps the meaning may lose the music, and the one who keeps the music may have to bend the meaning.

Yet the complaint can be pressed too far. Most readers meet the greater part of world literature in translation, and without translators the epics, novels and plays of other peoples would remain closed to them altogether. A good translation is not a copy of the original but a new work that answers to it, as a reply answers a letter. It may lose some things and gain others, and occasionally it becomes a classic in its own right. The fair question to ask of a translation is therefore not whether it is identical to the original, which no translation can be, but whether it gives its reader a living sense of why the original mattered.

questions.q: The central argument of the passage is that public libraries:
opts: are valuable chiefly because of the rare books they preserve.
should be replaced by digital services to save public money.
have lost their purpose now that facts are available on phones.
remain valuable as free public spaces and sources of guidance despite digital information.
questions.why: Main idea: the author rejects the 'relic' view and says digital information 'has, if anything, enlarged this role'.

questions.q: According to the passage, why are libraries often the first to lose staff and hours when budgets tighten?
opts: Librarians lack the skills needed for digital information.
Their buildings are too costly to maintain.
Readers have largely stopped visiting them.
Their benefits are diffuse and difficult to count.
questions.why: Detail: 'precisely because their benefits are diffuse and difficult to count'.

questions.q: With which of the following statements would the author most likely agree?
opts: Libraries should charge entry fees in order to survive.
Easy access to information does not by itself give people the ability to judge it.
Students from crowded homes prefer to study at home.
Search engines have made trained librarians unnecessary.
questions.why: Inference: 'A screen offers abundance but not guidance, and the skill of judging which sources deserve trust is not acquired automatically.'

questions.q: The author's attitude towards those who call the library a relic is best described as:
opts: fully in agreement with their view.
corrective, holding that they misunderstand what libraries do.
sympathetic, accepting that libraries are kept open out of sentiment.
questions.why: Tone: 'This view mistakes what libraries have always done.'

questions.q: As used in the passage, the word 'diffuse' means:
opts: spread thinly over many people rather than concentrated
questions.why: Vocabulary: the benefits are 'diffuse and difficult to count' because they are spread across many users in small ways.

questions.q: Which title best suits the passage?
opts: The Konkani Language and Its Rains
How to Become a Professional Translator
Why Poetry Can Never Be Translated
questions.why: Main idea: translation loses some things but gains others and opens world literature to readers.

questions.q: The example of the Konkani word for rain is used to illustrate that:
opts: English poetry lacks images drawn from nature.
Words carry associations that belong to one particular language.
Konkani has more words for rain than English does.
questions.why: Detail/illustration: words carry 'associations that belong to a single tongue'; the English equivalent 'summons umbrellas and grey streets'.

questions.q: It can be inferred that a reader who refuses to read anything in translation would:
opts: Be shut out of much of the world's literature.
questions.why: Inference: 'without translators the epics, novels and plays of other peoples would remain closed to them altogether'.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the author's position?
opts: Translation inevitably loses something, but a good one is a valuable work in its own right.
A translation should aim above all to be identical to its original.
Poetry should not be translated, since its meaning is always lost.
Translations matter only when they become classics.
questions.why: Attitude: 'the complaint can be pressed too far'; identity is something 'no translation can be'; the test is a 'living sense of why the original mattered'.

questions.q: In the phrase "a new work that answers to it", "answers to" most nearly means:
questions.why: Vocabulary: explained by the simile 'as a reply answers a letter'.

questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
opts: Mumbai, Delhi and, Chennai are big cities.
Mumbai, Delhi and Chennai are big cities.
Mumbai Delhi, and Chennai are big cities.
Mumbai, Delhi and Chennai, are big cities.
questions.why: Commas separate items in a list; none separates subject and verb. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “She is allergic ____ penicillin.”
questions.why: 'Allergic to'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “If she had taken the medicine on time, she ____ better now.”
questions.why: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The police tried to ____ a confession from the suspect.”
questions.why: 'Elicit' means to draw out; 'illicit' means unlawful. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “The secret must remain between you and I.”
questions.why: A preposition takes the objective case: 'between you and me'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Which team won the FIH Women's Hockey World Cup 2026?
questions.why: Argentina beat the Netherlands in a shootout after a 1-1 draw. Aug 2026.

questions.q: Former Uttar Pradesh Deputy CM Dinesh Sharma was sworn in in September 2026 as the Lieutenant Governor of:
questions.why: He replaced Admiral D. K. Joshi (retd), who had held the post since 2017. Sep 2026.

questions.q: On which date is International Literacy Day observed?
questions.why: Proclaimed by UNESCO in 1966; first observed 8 September 1967. Sep 2026.

questions.q: The 69th Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference, where Harivansh led India's delegation in September 2026, was held in:
questions.why: Canada will host the 70th conference in 2027. Oct 2026.

questions.q: India's first LNG-powered train was flagged off by Amit Shah on 27 September 2026 from:
questions.why: Its dual-fuel LNG-diesel system can replace about 40% of diesel use. Sep 2026.

questions.q: A Financial Emergency can be declared under Article:
questions.why: No Financial Emergency has ever been declared in India.

questions.q: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.why: He conducted the first general elections of 1951-52.

questions.q: The state tree of Goa is the:
questions.why: Matti is also called the crocodile-bark tree.

questions.q: UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2026, its 17th edition, is subtitled:
questions.why: It says the chance of staying below 1.5°C without overshoot is gone. Oct 2026.

questions.q: What was the theme of International Literacy Day 2026?
opts: Promoting literacy in the digital era
Literacy for people, the planet and prosperity
Literacy for a world in transition
questions.why: UNESCO's 2026 theme linked literacy to sustainable development. Sep 2026.

questions.q: What comes next? HIJ, KLM, NOP, QRS, …
questions.why: Each group starts 3 letters after the last one, with the same pattern inside: TUV. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks an item 10% above cost and gives a 20% discount. What is the overall gain?
questions.why: Net = (1 + 10/100)(1 − 20/100) − 1 = -12%. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 3, 7, 14, 24, 37, …
questions.why: The differences go up by 3 each time (4, 7, 10, 13, 16). Next: 53. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Find the wrong number in the series: 36, 49, 62, 77, 88, 101, 114
questions.why: In the correct series each term adds 13, so 77 should be 75. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Lata is the son of Deepak. Ajay is the daughter of Deepak. Neha is the husband of Ajay. How is Neha related to Lata?
questions.why: Draw the family tree from the statements; the answer is Brother-in-law. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Geeta walks 9 m West, then turns left and walks 2 m, then turns right and walks 3 m. Which direction is Geeta facing now?
questions.why: Follow each turn from the first direction: the last leg is towards the West. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 8:45?
questions.why: Angle = |30×8 − 5.5×45| = 7.5°. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In a group of 60 people, 34 like Konkani, 36 like Marathi and 3 like neither. How many like only Konkani?
questions.why: Both = 34 + 36 − (60 − 3) = 13; only Konkani = 34 − 13 = 21. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Anil's mother is the only daughter of Deepak's father. How is Deepak related to Anil if Deepak is a man?
questions.why: Draw the family tree from the statements; the answer is Maternal uncle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In a group of 80 people, 37 like tea, 37 like coffee and 27 like neither. How many like only tea?
questions.why: Both = 37 + 37 − (80 − 27) = 21; only tea = 37 − 21 = 16. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In selecting the homoeopathic remedy, which symptoms are of the least value?
opts: Common pathognomonic symptoms of the disease
Physical generals such as thermal reaction
questions.why: Pathognomonic symptoms belong to the disease, not the individual, so they rank lowest for remedy selection (§153, Kent).

questions.q: According to §71, the three points necessary for cure are knowledge of:
opts: the cause, the pathology and the prognosis of disease
the disease, the powers of medicines, and how to apply them
the miasm, the temperament and the diathesis
the diet, the regimen and the environment
questions.why: §71: the physician must learn what is to be cured in disease, the pathogenetic powers of medicines, and the mode of employing them.

questions.q: Pulsatilla nigricans is commonly known as:
questions.why: Pulsatilla nigricans (Ranunculaceae) is the wind flower or pasque flower; marsh tea is Ledum.

questions.q: Mental symptoms with a suicidal impulse following an injury to the head, in a patient worse in damp weather, call for:
questions.why: Natrum sulph: chronic effects of head injuries, mental troubles and suicidal tendency, aggravated by damp (Boericke).

questions.q: A patient who feels unusually well the day before an attack of illness, with marked chilliness and offensive discharges, needs:
questions.why: Psorinum (Allen's Keynotes): feels unusually well the day before an attack.

questions.q: A potency labelled '200K' has been prepared by:
questions.why: The suffix K marks potencies made by Korsakov's single-vial method.

questions.q: Before the HPI was published, Indian manufacturers mainly followed:
opts: the American (HPUS) and German homoeopathic pharmacopoeias
the Indian Pharmacopoeia of allopathic drugs
questions.why: Until the HPI appeared, Indian firms worked to the Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia of the United States and the German pharmacopoeia.

questions.q: The rubric 'Mind, Ennui' means:
questions.why: Ennui is boredom or tedium.

questions.q: A patient says, 'Nobody cares for me; I am all alone in this world.' The best rubric is:
questions.why: The feeling of being isolated and uncared for is rubric-converted to 'Forsaken feeling'.

questions.q: Most of the carbon dioxide in blood is carried as:
questions.why: About 70% of CO₂ is carried as bicarbonate formed by carbonic anhydrase in red cells.

questions.q: The clearance of para-aminohippuric acid (PAH) is used to measure:
questions.why: PAH is filtered and secreted so completely that its clearance approximates renal plasma flow.

questions.q: A rubbery intravascular clot with a dark-red dependent 'currant-jelly' part and a yellow 'chicken-fat' upper part, not attached to the vessel wall, is a:
questions.why: Post-mortem clots form after death as red cells settle, giving currant-jelly and chicken-fat layers; they lack lines of Zahn and wall attachment.

questions.q: On abdominal ultrasonography, fatty liver typically appears as a liver with:
opts: A shrunken nodular outline with ascites
questions.why: Fat in hepatocytes increases reflectivity, so the liver looks brighter than the kidney cortex; a small nodular liver with ascites suggests cirrhosis.

questions.q: In the Weil-Felix test, agglutination of the Proteus OX-K strain alone suggests:
questions.why: Orientia tsutsugamushi gives OX-K agglutination; epidemic and endemic typhus react with OX-19, and Q fever is Weil-Felix negative.

questions.q: A very high blood pressure is termed a hypertensive emergency, rather than urgency, when there is:
opts: A diastolic BP above 120 mmHg without symptoms
Failure to respond to three antihypertensive drugs
questions.why: A hypertensive emergency is severe BP elevation with acute organ damage (encephalopathy, LVF, dissection, AKI); without it the situation is urgency.

questions.q: A chronic, itchy eczema of the antecubital and popliteal fossae in a young adult with a personal history of asthma and hay fever is most likely:
questions.why: Atopic eczema affects the flexures in older children and adults and is associated with asthma and allergic rhinitis; psoriasis favours extensor surfaces.

questions.q: Urticaria with burning, itching blotches following the eating of shellfish calls for:
questions.why: Urtica urens has burning, stinging urticaria and is noted for ailments from eating shellfish.

questions.q: A primigravida usually first perceives fetal movements (quickening) at about:
questions.why: Quickening is felt at about 20 weeks in a primigravida and about 2 weeks earlier in a multigravida.

questions.q: Red (carneous) degeneration of a fibroid most often occurs:
opts: during pregnancy, usually in the second trimester
in the first year after menarche
during lactation after the sixth month
questions.why: Red degeneration is a haemorrhagic infarction typically seen in mid-pregnancy, causing acute pain and fever.

questions.q: Under the national programme, the first dose of vitamin A given at 9 months of age is:
questions.why: The first dose is 1 lakh IU at 9 months with MR; later doses are 2 lakh IU every 6 months up to 5 years.

questions.q: A full-thickness (third-degree) burn is typically:
opts: moist and pink with intact sensation
questions.why: Full-thickness burns destroy the nerve endings, so the area is insensate, white or charred and leathery.

questions.q: The commonest bacterial cause of acute otitis media is:
questions.why: S. pneumoniae, then H. influenzae and Moraxella, cause most AOM; Pseudomonas and Proteus are typical of CSOM.

questions.q: A blue line along the gum margins (Burtonian line) is a sign of chronic poisoning by:
questions.why: The Burtonian line is lead sulphide deposited at the gum margin in chronic lead poisoning.

questions.q: The dependency ratio is calculated as:
opts: population aged 65 and above / total population
questions.why: The dependency ratio relates the economically dependent young and old to the working-age population of 15-64 years.

questions.q: The population norm for one Primary Health Centre in hilly, tribal or difficult areas is:
questions.why: A PHC covers 30,000 in plains and 20,000 in hilly or tribal areas; 80,000 is the CHC norm for hilly areas.
